name: Subhuman / LTN / HTN / Chad tiers
lead: Subhuman, LTN, HTN and Chad are labels in a tier system used in looksmaxxing and incel communities to rank men's physical attractiveness. LTN and HTN stand for low-tier normie and high-tier normie.[1] The system descends from a rating scale developed on defunct forums.[1]

Wikipedia's article on looksmaxxing describes seven categories in the PSL (Perceived Sexual Levels) scale, which rates facial attractiveness on a 1 to 8 scale and is built around assumptions about how women perceive men, with the lowest category called 'subhuman' or 'sub-3'.[1] Another description of the scene, associated with the streamer Clavicular, uses three tiers: subhuman, normie and Chad.[1] Researchers and critics consider parts of the PSL system pseudoscientific.[1]

paras: Chad is slang from manosphere forums for an attractive, sexually successful man, and appears as a rank in PSL categories including 'Chadlite' and 'giga Chad'.[1][2] Normie describes an average-looking person; the spelled-out forms low-tier normie and high-tier normie subdivide the middle range.[1][2] Subhuman denotes the lowest PSL category.[1] Stacy and Becky are the corresponding terms for attractive and less attractive women.[2]

The vocabulary and rating scale were developed on forums named in coverage as PUAHate.com, Sluthate.com and Lookism.net, collectively the PSL forums, which are now defunct.[1] Looksmaxxing itself was spread to wider audiences by TikTok in the early 2020s.[1]

Writer Becca Rothfeld criticised, in The New Yorker in March 2026, the practice of labelling any person subhuman.[1] The scheme is regarded by researchers as lacking scientific grounding, in part because it rates only the face and is based on assumed female preferences.[1]

timeline.event: Looksmaxxing term coined on incel message boards; PSL forums develop the rating vocabulary.[1]
TikTok spreads looksmaxxing language to wider audiences.[1]

card.summary: The ranking vocabulary of looksmaxxing: from subhuman through LTN and HTN to Chad, descended from the PSL scale.
card.note: Researchers consider parts of the PSL system pseudoscientific; critics object to dehumanising labels.

quick.overview:
Tier language ranks men by perceived looks. The bottom is 'subhuman', the middle splits into low-tier and high-tier normie, and the top is Chad, with further steps like giga Chad.

The system descends from the PSL scale, which scores facial attractiveness from 1 to 8.
quick.mechanism: It is a shared vocabulary, not a procedure. Members rate faces against the scale, often in forum photo threads.
quick.risks: Critics note the labels can be dehumanising and that the scale has no scientific validation; effects on self-image have not been formally studied in the sources reviewed.
